title: Collaborative Work Management Technologies and Managerial Intensity in U.S. Corporations: An Examination
authors: Piyush Gulati; Arianna Marchetti; Phanish Puranam
near_miss_reason: Underlying design is staggered binary CWM adoption by firm-year (2010-2019), but every reported regression (Tables 4-6, Figure 4) is a stacked DiD: adopters paired with within-NAICS2 non-adopters in event-time stacks, CEM-matched, with stack-by-firm and stack-by-year FE, CEM frequency weights, and time-varying firm controls (return_on_assets, segment_count, log_emp, log_age_yrs) in all columns. Dropping controls would still leave a stacked design, which PROTOCOL Sec. 2 excludes, so it is recorded as ineligible rather than a controls-only near miss.
eligible_reason: Stacked design with time-varying controls and matching weights in every reported column; no unstacked TWFE on the firm-year panel is reported (1-panel-data-analyses.do only plots year-FE trends by treated status for Figures 2-3, 5).
design_notes: Firm-year panel of 3,017 Compustat firms 2010-2019 with managerial intensity (Revelio), decentralization scores (Lightcast job postings) and CWM adoption year (treated_yr_cwm). 11-panel-to-stacked.py builds stacks; 12-coarsened-exact-matching.do CEM on pre-period averages; 2-matched-data-analyses.do: reghdfe y i.post_cwm##i.treated controls [aw=freq_weight], absorb(stack_firm stack_year) vce(cluster firm) for Tables 4-6; Figure 4 event study ib4.treated_timeline_pos##i.treated with the same FE and controls. No csdid/did_imputation code despite full-text Callaway mention. README states data_final/*.csv are disguised.
estimators_reported: stacked DiD with CEM weights and controls (reghdfe)
data_files: data_final/panel-data-final.csv (2.7 MB), data_final/matched-data-final.csv (53 MB), *-balance-check.csv -- README: 'disguised data files ... to enable execution of the STATA scripts'
software_notes: Stata (reghdfe, cem, coefplot, estout) for tables; Python for raw data construction (Lightcast, Revelio, Compustat; licensed)
